priceScope: Whole-organization cost per learner against randomized earnings gains at the Bronx site; income-only welfare comparison, not a verified marginal gift offer

what: Per Scholas, founded in the Bronx, runs free, full-time technology training courses for adults who are unemployed or in low-wage work.
It now trains over 4,600 learners a year at more than 20 campuses, and helps graduates find jobs with employer partners.
This in-depth review prices the organization’s whole cost per learner against earnings gains from the randomized WorkAdvance trial at its Bronx site.
strengths: In a randomized trial of about 690 Bronx applicants, Per Scholas raised earnings in years 2–5 and 7–8; in year 6 participants earned $6,281 (20%) more than the control group.
Arnold Ventures rates the program Near Top Tier, and its effects were the strongest of the four WorkAdvance providers.
The trial cost only about $5,700 per participant to run, low for job training.
reservations: Our working estimate is about $903K per better life; all of it is income, and by year 10 the earnings gain had disappeared.
Today’s whole-organization cost is about $13,497 per learner, more than double the trial’s inflation-adjusted cost, after rapid expansion to over 20 campuses.
The three other WorkAdvance providers showed no lasting effect, so the result may not transfer to every campus or to today’s curriculum.

sections.what: Per Scholas (Per Scholas Inc, EIN 04-3252955) offers free, full-time technology courses, mainly in IT, to adults who are unemployed or in low-wage work. It works with employers on curricula and hiring. Founded in the Bronx, it now operates more than 20 metro campuses. It reported over 4,600 learners and more than 2,600 graduates in 2023. A donation supports the whole organization.
sections.monitoring: Per Scholas was one of four providers in MDRC’s WorkAdvance randomized trial, which randomly assigned 2,564 applicants in 2011–13; about 690 were at the Per Scholas Bronx site. Earnings come from administrative wage records, now followed for ten years. Per Scholas publishes annual reports with learner counts and placement wages. We did not find New York-only learner counts or a current cost per learner; we have not contacted the organization.
sections.qualitative: The Per Scholas site produced the strongest effects in WorkAdvance: earnings rose in years 2 to 5 and 7 to 8, with a year-6 gain of $6,281 (20%) over a $32,122 control mean. MDRC’s 10-year report (2025) found no year-10 effect at Per Scholas, while St. Nicks Alliance, another New York provider, showed later gains. The other two sites showed only short-lived effects. Arnold Ventures rates Per Scholas Near Top Tier. The trial version included post-placement advancement coaching; today’s larger, multi-campus program may differ.
sections.cost:
Our central estimate is **$903K per better life**, using ten healthy-year welfare equivalents. It is an income-only comparison: we credit no health gain.

**Cost.** CY2023 total expense was $62.1M for about 4,600 learners: $13,497 each, for the whole organization. In the trial, operating cost was about $5,700 per participant (net $3,500 after services controls received), or about $7,524 today.

**Benefit.** We credit an average gross gain of $5,000 a year in years 2–8, between the significant early gains and the year-6 peak of $6,281, and nothing after, because the year-10 effect was zero. 60% counts as net household welfare, on a $32,000 base. We keep 0.7 for transfer to today’s program, 0.85 for displacement and 0.9 for NYC residence.

**Range.** At the trial cost the estimate is $503K per better life. Using the year-6 gain throughout gives $727K per better life; a $3,000 average gives $1.48M per better life; halving the transfer gives $1.81M per better life. If the trial effect does not hold at current scale, there is no credited benefit.
sections.funding: Per Scholas reported CY2023 revenue of $83.3M, including $63.5M of contributions and $17.8M of program service revenue, and expenses of $62.1M, up from $55.0M in 2022 and $36.1M in 2021. Training is free to learners; funding comes from philanthropy, employers and public workforce grants. We have not seen a costed plan for added New York learners.

model.costScope: CY2023 whole-organization expense divided by about 4,600 learners.
model.geographicAttribution: NYC-metro learners; 0.9 of earning years in the metro.
model.formula: Price = 10 × cost per learner ÷ [0.5 × discounted years(2–8) × ln(1 + 0.6 × gain ÷ base) × transfer × non-displacement × NYC share]. Health = 0.
model.counterfactual: Randomized control applicants with access to other training and jobs.
model.attribution: A gift is credited with the transferred average effect of an added learner at whole-organization average cost; whether a gift adds a New York learner is unverified.
model.uncertainty: Dominated by transfer from the 2011–13 Bronx site to today’s scaled program and by current cost per learner.
model.nativeOutcomes: Annual earnings in years 1–10 from wage records; year-10 effect null.
